subject: English
source: Tarbiyyah Primary English scheme of work for Moon Zoom! (the school's own adaptation of the Cornerstones English unit) for the Friday writing; Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised (named by phase and unit only) for phonics; National Curriculum Year 1 English. Spring 1 founding year (11 Jan to 8 Feb 2027) includes the bridge weeks.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Revising our sounds and writing sentences
lessons.title: Bismillah, sound review and the sounds h, b, f
objectives: Recall the sounds learned in Reception
Learn the sounds h, b and f and read words with them

keywords.def: what we hear and say for a letter
push sounds together to read a word

starter: Say the sounds: s a t p i n m d
Say the tricky words: I, the, to, no, go

teach.heading: Bismillah and sound review
teach.note: Start with bismillah. Hold up cards for s a t p i n m d g o c k ck e u r; children say the sound as quickly as they can. Note any child who hesitates for extra practice later.

teach.heading: New sound h
bullets: Say a puff of air: h
teach.note: Say a breathy h with no vowel. Ask children to feel their breath on their hand. Show the picture of a hat. Write h: down the tall stick, up, over the arch.

teach.heading: New sounds b and f
bullets: b has a bat and a ball
teach.note: b and d are often reversed: b has a stick first then the ball (bat then ball). f: down the stick, curl over, cross. Say f as a long ffff with teeth on lip.

teach.heading: Read the new words
teach.note: Sound-talk each word and blend. Show how swapping the first sound changes the word: hat - bat - fat. Encourage children to say the new word each time.

practice: Read the words: hot, bit, fun, hen
Sound-talk and say: b-e-d, h-a-t, f-a-n
Write the words hot, bed, fun on a whiteboard
independent: Write and read: a big bed, a hot hen
Draw a picture of a hat and label it with letters you know
lessons.homework: Read the words hat, bed, fun to someone at home.
lessons.send: SEND: use letter tiles and sound-button cards. EAL: link each word to a picture. Stretch: write a sentence: The hen is on the bed.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Revising our sounds and writing sentences
lessons.title: Double letters: ff, ll, ss
objectives: Learn that ff, ll and ss make one sound at the end of words
Read and write words like huff, bell, hill, miss

keywords.def: two of the same letter that make one sound, like ll in bell

starter: Say the sounds h b f l

teach.heading: Double letters, one sound
bullets: Found at the end of words
teach.note: Explain that sometimes two of the same letter go together to make one sound. Show words: puff, bell, hiss. Children tap the sounds on fingers: p-u-ff (3 sounds) not 4.

teach.heading: Read ff words
teach.note: Sound-talk: h-u-ff. Show sound buttons: dots under h and u, bar under ff. Read and repeat. Note: ‘of’ is a tricky word, different from ‘off’.

teach.heading: Read ll and ss words
teach.note: Group by pattern. Read ll words first, then ss. Explain the rule of thumb: we double f, l and s after a short vowel in short words (the FLOSS rule). Do not over-explain; show and practise.

teach.heading: Write the words
teach.note: Model writing ‘bell’ with three sounds; the final ll counts as one sound. Children write bell, hill, miss. Check double letter formation.

practice: Read and match: bell, hill, miss, puff with pictures
Write these words as I say them: doll, off, moss
independent: Sort words into three sets: ff, ll, ss (puff, bell, hiss, huff, hill, miss, off, doll)
Write a sentence with a double-letter word: I can hiss like a snake.
lessons.homework: Write three double-letter words and read them to a grown-up.
lessons.send: SEND: use highlighted double letters. EAL: practise ss/ll with picture cards. Stretch: write sentences using three of the words.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Revising our sounds and writing sentences
lessons.title: Reading and writing words with double letters
objectives: Read sentences with ff, ll and ss words
Write a sentence using a double-letter word

keywords.def: a group of words that makes sense

starter: Read tricky words: I, the, to, no, go

teach.heading: Sound-talk the sentence
bullets: The bell is on the hill.
teach.note: Display the sentence. Children sound-talk any tricky word, then read in full. Re-read to practise fluency.

teach.heading: Capital letters and full stops
teach.note: Point out the capital T and the full stop. Ask: How many words? Count them aloud. Model finger spaces by placing a finger between words.

teach.heading: Write a sentence
teach.note: Model: ‘The cat sat on the mat.’ Say it, hold up fingers for each word, then write. Emphasise rereading to check.

teach.heading: Check it
teach.note: Use a checklist: capital, finger spaces, full stop. Show two examples; let children say what is good and what could be better.

practice: Read: The bell is on the hill.
Read three sentences with a partner
Write the sentence: The doll is off.
independent: Write two sentences about a picture of a hill and bell
Check each sentence with the checklist
lessons.homework: Write a sentence about a bell and read it to someone at home.
lessons.send: SEND: sentence strips and word bank. EAL: label picture with key words first. Stretch: add the word ‘because’ in a sentence.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Revising our sounds and writing sentences
lessons.title: Tricky words: he, she, we, me, be
objectives: Read and spell the tricky words he, she, we, me, be
Use them in sentences

keywords.def: a word where some letters do not make the sound we expect

starter: Read: I, the, to, no, go
Sound-talk: sh-e (we have not learned sh yet!)

teach.heading: The ‘e’ says its name
teach.note: In these words the letter e says its name /ee/. Show each word. Children say the sounds with the tricky part highlighted, e.g. h-e (with e underlined). Reading list: he, we, me, be.

teach.heading: The word she
teach.note: The word ‘she’ has the sh sound (not yet learned). Explain simply: s and h together make /sh/ (like when we say shh). Then e says its name. Preview of next week’s sounds.

teach.heading: Use them in sentences
teach.note: Read each sentence with children. Pause on the tricky word. Link to adab: ‘Be kind’, treat others with kindness. Children say which word is tricky.

teach.heading: Spelling tricky words
teach.note: Teach the look-say-cover-write-check routine. Children try he and we on whiteboards. Praise careful checking.

practice: Read the tricky word cards fast
Say the sentence: He can run.
Read sentences: She can run. We go to the hill. Be kind to me.
Spell he, we, me on whiteboards
independent: Write a sentence using he or she and a picture of someone doing an action
Read your sentence to your partner
exit: Which letter says its name in ‘he’?
lessons.homework: Practise reading he, she, we, me, be with a grown-up.
lessons.send: SEND: reduce to 2-3 words and use colour on the tricky part. EAL: use pictures for he/she. Stretch: write 3 sentences with different words.

lessons.title: Bridge writing: a recount of my first week with capital letters, finger spaces and full stops
lessons.bigQuestion: What does a sentence need so that a reader can read it?
objectives: To say, write and read back a sentence about a real event
successCriteria: All: write one sentence with a capital letter and a full stop
Most: write three sentences in time order with finger spaces
Some: join two ideas with and
lessons.crossCurricular: PSHE: talking about a new school and new friends
lessons.smsc: Social: sharing news kindly and listening to others (adab of listening)

islamicLink.text: Sharing news kindly and listening to others (adab of listening)

keywords.def: writing that tells what happened, in order
a big letter at the start of a sentence
a dot that ends a sentence
a gap between words

hook.text: thisweekimetmynewteacher. What is wrong? How many fixes can you spot?
hook.a: No capital letter, no spaces, no full stop: This week I met my new teacher.

pictures.alt: pencil and lined paper for writing

resources: Slides
Mini-whiteboard and pen
Lined paper or exercise book
Sentence checker card: capital, spaces, full stop
Phase 5 sound mat

starter.q: Write the capital letter for i
What goes at the end of a sentence?

teach.heading: Three rules for a sentence
teach.note: What is a recount?: It tells what happened; It is in time order; It says I and we. Explain a recount tells a real event in order. Today we recount our first week at TGA (induction week). Show the rules on the checker card. Pupils touch head (capital), hold up a finger (space), point (full stop).

teach.heading: Say, count, write, read
teach.note: Model the routine aloud with one sentence. Touch each word as you read back.

model.problem: Write: I met my new class.
steps: Write with a finger space after each word

teach.heading: Time words
teach.note: Time words put the recount in order. Model: First I logged in. Next I met my teacher. Then I read a book.

teach.heading: Hinge: which is right?
teach.note: Show me A, B or C on the whiteboard.

check.why: B has a capital, spaces and a full stop. A has no capital, C has no space and no full stop.

practice.q: Fix it: i read a book
practice.model: Teacher works this one aloud: read the question, underline the key words, link it to today's rule, then give the answer in a full sentence: I read a book.

practice.q: Put in order: Then I read. First I logged in.
practice.a: First I logged in. Then I read.

independent.q: Core: write 2 sentences about your first week
independent.a: For example: First I met my teacher. Then I read a book.
independent.model: Labelled model to go through first (Write: I met my new class.): Say it out loud | Count the words: 5 | Write with a finger space after each word | Add the full stop | Read it back | Result: I met my new class.

independent.q: Extend: write 3 sentences with First, Next, Then
independent.a: For example: First I said salaam. Next I met my class. Then I played a game.

independent.q: Stretch: join two ideas with and
independent.a: For example: I met my teacher and I read a book.

exit.q: What three things does a sentence need?
exit.a: a capital letter, finger spaces, a full stop

lessons.homework: Tell an adult one thing you did this week in a full sentence, then write it with a capital letter and a full stop.
lessons.send: SEND: sentence strip with word boxes; teacher scribes the first word. EAL: rehearse each sentence aloud twice before writing. Stretch: use and to join ideas and add one describing word.

lessons.title: Sounds j and v
objectives: Learn the sounds j and v
Read and write words with j and v

keywords.def: the sound at the start of jam
the sound at the start of van

starter: Say the sounds: h b f l

teach.heading: The sound j
teach.note: Teach j: a short, voiced sound, not ‘juh’. Show picture of jam. Writing: down, curl left, then a dot on top.

teach.heading: The sound v
teach.note: v: place top teeth on bottom lip and hum. Do not say ‘vuh’. Writing: a sharp down and up v shape.

teach.heading: Read words
teach.note: Sound-talk each word. Mix in older words. Ask: ‘Which words start with j? v?’ Children point and read.

teach.heading: Write words
teach.note: Model writing ‘jam’ and ‘van’. Children write jet, vet and one of their own.

practice: Say the sound for each letter: j v h b
independent: Write a caption for each picture: a jug, a van, a vet
Read your captions to a friend
lessons.homework: Find something that starts with j or v at home and write its name.
lessons.send: SEND: use tactile letters. EAL: use picture cards. Stretch: write sentences: The vet has a van.

lessons.title: Sounds w and x
objectives: Learn the sounds w and x
Read and write words with w and x

keywords.def: the sound at the start of web
two sounds together, /k/ and /s/, as in box

starter: Sounds: j v h b f

teach.heading: The sound w
teach.note: Make lips round to say /w/. Not ‘wuh’. Writing: a down-up-down-up zig-zag. Show the web picture.

teach.heading: The sound x
teach.note: x is two sounds, /k/ and /s/, but we write one letter. In words x is at the end: fox, box, six. Count the sounds in fox: f-o-x (3).

teach.heading: Read words
teach.note: Sound-talk and read. Group by w words and x words. Compare ‘wig’ and ‘win’. Ask: ‘Where is the x in fox?’

teach.heading: Write words
teach.note: Model fox and box. Check that x is formed correctly with two crossing lines. Children write six and wig.

practice: Read the words and match to the pictures: web, wig, box, fox
independent: Write sentences: I can win. The fox is in the box.
Draw a fox in a box and label it
lessons.homework: Write six w or x words and read them to a grown-up.
lessons.send: SEND: use word-picture matching. EAL: pair words with actions. Stretch: write a sentence with two w words.

lessons.title: Sounds y, z, zz and qu
objectives: Learn the sounds y, z, zz and qu
Read words like yes, zip, buzz, quit

keywords.def: two z letters that make one sound at the end of a word
two letters that make the sound /kw/

teach.heading: The sound y
teach.note: Teach y at the start of words as /y/. Do not say ‘yuh’. Writing: two strokes forming a v with a tail.

teach.heading: The sounds z and zz
teach.note: z at the start of a word. zz is a double letter at the end: buzz, fizz. Count sounds: b-u-zz (3). Compare with ss/ff/ll.

teach.heading: The sound qu
teach.note: q is never alone; it is always followed by u. Together they make /kw/. Show quiz, quit, quick. Children write q first, then u.

teach.heading: Read and write words
teach.note: Read the words, then dictate: yes, zip, buzz. Ask children to write quiz. Check q and u order.

practice: Read: yes, yet, zip, buzz, quiz, quick
independent: Write a caption for each picture: a zip, a bee that buzzes, a quiz
Read a sentence: Yes, I can zip it.
exit: Which letter always comes with q?
lessons.homework: Look for q, y or z in words around your home.
lessons.send: SEND: use highlighted qu. EAL: pair with actions: zip it, buzz. Stretch: write 2 sentences with qu words.

lessons.title: Digraphs ch and sh
objectives: Learn that ch and sh each make one sound
Read and write words like chip, shop, chat, fish

keywords.def: two letters that make one sound

teach.heading: What is a digraph?
teach.note: Define digraph as two letters making one sound. Show ch, sh. Reinforce earlier ones: ck, ff, ll, ss, zz, qu. Ask children to name other digraphs they know.

teach.heading: The digraph ch
bullets: Like a train: ch ch ch
teach.note: Make a train noise. Show words and underline ch with a line. Sound-talk: ch-i-p (3 sounds) not c-h-i-p.

teach.heading: The digraph sh
teach.note: Finger to lips for sh. Sound-talk: sh-o-p. Include fish and dish where sh is at the end. Compare ship and chip.

teach.heading: Read and write
teach.note: Read the words. Then write ‘chop’ and ‘ship’ with sound buttons. Remind children each digraph is one sound, so two letters share one sound button.

practice: Sound-talk and read: ch-e-ck, sh-e-d, ch-i-n
independent: Sort words: ch or sh (chip, ship, chat, shop, fish, chin, dish, check)
Write a sentence: She had fish and chips.
exit: How many letters and how many sounds in ‘chip’?
lessons.homework: Find ch or sh words at home (e.g. fish, chips) and write one.
lessons.send: SEND: use coloured digraph cards. EAL: link to food words. Stretch: write 2 sentences with ch and sh.

lessons.title: Digraphs th, ng and nk
objectives: Learn th, ng and nk
Read and write words like this, thin, ring, sink

keywords.def: two letters that make /th/ with tongue between teeth
two letters that make one sound at the end of a word
n and k together at the end of a word

teach.heading: The digraph th
teach.note: th has two sounds: voiced (this, that) and unvoiced (thin, thud). At this stage just teach /th/ and model both. Tongue gently between teeth.

teach.heading: The digraph ng
teach.note: ng is a single sound. Ask children to hold the sound: ‘nnng’. Sound-talk: r-i-ng (3 sounds). Not r-i-n-g.

teach.heading: nk at the end
teach.note: nk is not a digraph; it blends the two sounds /ng/ /k/. Sound-talk: p-i-n-k (4 sounds, the n makes /ng/). Keep it simple: just read.

teach.heading: Read and write
teach.note: Read the words, then dictate: thin, king, pink. Check ng and nk. Link to context: king, ring, sink etc.

practice: Sound-talk and read: th-a-t, l-o-ng, b-a-nk
independent: Write sentences: The king has a ring. The ring is in the sink.
Sort words: th / ng / nk
lessons.homework: Practise reading th, ng and nk words with a grown-up.
lessons.send: SEND: use cards with the digraph highlighted. EAL: model th with mirror. Stretch: write 3 sentences using th, ng and nk words.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Long vowel sounds ai, ee, igh, oa, oo
lessons.title: The vowel digraph ai
objectives: Learn that ai makes the sound /ai/ as in rain
Read and write words with ai

keywords.def: two letters that together make one vowel sound
water that falls from clouds

teach.heading: Meet ai
teach.note: Show the picture of rain. Say the word, stretch the vowel sound: r-ai-n. Draw sound buttons: dot under r, bar under ai, dot under n. Note ai is usually found in the middle of words, not at the end.

teach.heading: Read ai words
teach.note: Sound-talk each word, blend. Ask children to say how many sounds are in ‘snail’ (s-n-ai-l, 4 sounds). Point out each digraph is a single sound.

teach.heading: Write ai words
bullets: Write a letter for each sound
teach.note: Model writing ‘rain’ and ‘train’. Children try ‘tail’ and ‘mail’. Remind them: ai in the middle of words.

teach.heading: ai in a sentence
bullets: The snail is in the rain.
teach.note: Read the sentence with expression. Point to capital letter and full stop. Ask: ‘Where is the ai?’ Children underline it.

practice: Read and match to pictures: rain, snail, train, nail
independent: Write a sentence about a snail in the rain
Underline the ai in each word
exit: Which two letters make /ai/ in rain?
lessons.homework: Find or draw something with an ai sound and write its name.
lessons.send: SEND: use highlighted digraph cards. EAL: repeat key words aloud. Stretch: write a caption with two ai words.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Long vowel sounds ai, ee, igh, oa, oo
lessons.title: The vowel digraph ee
objectives: Learn that ee makes the sound /ee/ as in feet
Read and write words with ee

keywords.def: two e letters that make the long /ee/ sound

teach.heading: Meet ee
teach.note: Show the picture of feet. Say f-ee-t. Children hold their feet and say ‘ee’. Contrast with the short e in egg. Sound buttons: dot f, bar ee, dot t.

teach.heading: Read ee words
teach.note: Sound-talk and blend each word. Ask: ‘Where is the ee: start, middle or end?’ It can be in the middle (feet) or at the end (see, bee, tree).

teach.heading: Write ee words
teach.note: Model sheep and tree. Dictate: seed, green. Check that children use ee not ea at this stage.

teach.heading: ee in sentences
bullets: I can see a green tree.
teach.note: Read the sentence together and ask children to find the ee words (see, green, tree). Reread with expression.

practice: Read the words: sheep, seed, week, green
independent: Write two sentences with ee words (e.g. I see a bee.)
Draw a green tree and label it
lessons.homework: Look for ee words at home and read them.
lessons.send: SEND: use picture-word matching. EAL: pair ee words with actions (e.g. peep). Stretch: write a caption for a picture of a sheep in a field.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Long vowel sounds ai, ee, igh, oa, oo
lessons.title: The trigraph igh
objectives: Learn that igh makes the sound /igh/ as in night
Read and write words with igh

keywords.def: three letters that make one sound

teach.heading: Meet igh
teach.note: Define trigraph: three letters, one sound. Show night: n-igh-t (3 sounds). The bar goes under igh. Children say the sound as you point.

teach.heading: Read igh words
teach.note: Sound-talk: l-igh-t. Read the list, mixing in earlier sounds: sigh, fight, tight. Ask: ‘Which letters do you read as one sound?’

teach.heading: Write igh words
bullets: Write l, then igh, then t
teach.note: Model writing light. The common error is to write it as ‘lite’ (a common spelling mistake). Remind: igh makes /igh/ in light, night, right.

teach.heading: igh in sentences
teach.note: Read sentences together. Point to igh. Talk about the night sky, the moon and the stars and the beauty of what Allah has made.

independent: Write sentences: The moon is high. The light is bright.
Draw the night sky and label it using igh words
exit: How many letters make the /igh/ sound?
lessons.homework: Practise reading and writing night, light and high.
lessons.send: SEND: use colour on igh. EAL: pair with pictures. Stretch: write a sentence using three igh words.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Long vowel sounds ai, ee, igh, oa, oo
lessons.title: The vowel digraph oa
objectives: Learn that oa makes the sound /oa/ as in boat
Read and write words with oa

keywords.def: two letters that make the long /oa/ sound

teach.heading: Meet oa
teach.note: Show a picture of a boat. Say b-oa-t and have children rock like a boat. Highlight oa as the middle sound; it is usually found in the middle of words.

teach.heading: Read oa words
teach.note: Sound-talk and blend, e.g. r-oa-d. Ask about meaning: ‘What do you wear in winter?’ (coat). Keep reading brisk.

teach.heading: Write oa words
teach.note: Model soap and toast. Dictate: float, goal. Remind children that oa is mostly in the middle; the end of a word often uses ow or o (but that is later).

teach.heading: oa in sentences
bullets: The goat is on the road.
teach.note: Read sentences with children. Ask them to find oa words and underline them. Check they are reading with correct sound.

independent: Write a sentence about a goat on a boat
Draw and label a boat, a coat and a goat
exit: Which two letters make /oa/ in boat?
lessons.homework: Find oa words in a book or on packaging.
lessons.send: SEND: use matching picture cards. EAL: act out words (float, toast). Stretch: write a sentence using three oa words.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Long vowel sounds ai, ee, igh, oa, oo
lessons.title: The vowel digraph oo (long and short)
objectives: Learn that oo can make a long sound (zoo) and a short sound (book)
Read and write oo words

keywords.def: two letters that can make a long sound as in moon or a short sound as in book

teach.heading: Two sounds for oo
teach.note: Teach that oo can say two sounds. Say zoo and book. Children try both sounds on an unknown word and choose the one that makes a real word. Use a coloured sound-button or a different icon for long vs short.

teach.heading: Long oo words
teach.note: Sound-talk the long oo words. Ask: ‘Which words belong in the kitchen?’ (spoon, food). Link with adab: eating with the right hand and saying bismillah before food.

teach.heading: Short oo words
teach.note: Sound-talk the short oo words. Read a sentence: ‘Look at the good book.’ Note: the choice is made by trying both sounds.

teach.heading: Write oo words
teach.note: Model moon and book. Dictate: zoo, look. Children check by reading back which sound they used.

practice: Which words have the long oo? Which have the short?
Read and sort: spoon, good, look, food, foot, zoo
independent: Write two sentences: I look at the moon. I read a good book.
Draw a zoo and label it
exit: Read: food. Is it long oo or short oo?
lessons.homework: Read your favourite book to someone at home.
lessons.send: SEND: use two-colour sound buttons. EAL: practise both oo sounds with a mirror. Stretch: write three sentences with oo.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: More vowel sounds and writing a story
lessons.title: The vowel digraphs ar and or
objectives: Learn ar as in car and or as in fork
Read and write words with ar and or

keywords.def: the sound in car
the sound in fork

teach.heading: Meet ar
bullets: Say it with a wide mouth
teach.note: Show car. Say c-ar. Have children open their mouths wide, like at the doctor. Sound buttons: bar under ar.

teach.heading: Meet or
teach.note: Show or in fork: f-or-k. Contrast ar and or by saying car vs core. Children read the words in pairs.

teach.heading: Read ar and or words
teach.note: Sound-talk each word: p-ar-k. Ask children to say which sound they hear. Mix both groups at speed.

teach.heading: Write ar and or words
teach.note: Model card and corn. Dictate: farm, fork, start. Remind children to use sound buttons to check.

practice: Sort words: ar or or (farm, fork, start, corn, card, born)
independent: Write sentences: I go to the farm in a car. I eat corn with a fork.
Draw a farm and label it
exit: Which letters make the sound in car?
lessons.homework: Look for ar or or words around your home.
lessons.send: SEND: use picture cards for sort. EAL: practise vowel sounds with mirror. Stretch: write three sentences with ar and or.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: More vowel sounds and writing a story
lessons.title: The vowel digraphs ur and ow
objectives: Learn ur as in burn and ow as in cow
Read and write words with ur and ow

keywords.def: the sound in burn
the sound in cow

teach.heading: Meet ur
teach.note: Show burn. b-ur-n has 3 sounds. Ask children to listen: the same sound is in fur, curl, purple. Sound buttons: bar under ur.

teach.heading: Meet ow
teach.note: Say ‘Ow!’ and show cow. ow is usually at the end or in the middle: cow, down. Note: ow has a second sound in snow; learn later.

teach.heading: Read ur and ow words
teach.note: Sound-talk and blend. Ask: ‘Which words have ur? Which have ow?’ Include sentence: ‘The brown cow went down.’

teach.heading: Write ur and ow words
teach.note: Model writing brown and turn. Dictate: town, hurt. Remind children to check the digraph by reading it back.

independent: Write sentences: The cow is brown. I turn down the road.
Draw a brown cow and label it
exit: Which sound do ur and ow make?
lessons.homework: Practise reading ur and ow words at home.
lessons.send: SEND: use picture cards. EAL: pair with actions (turn, down). Stretch: write a short caption with ur and ow words.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: More vowel sounds and writing a story
lessons.title: The vowel digraphs oi and ear
objectives: Learn oi as in coin and ear as in hear
Read and write words with oi and ear

keywords.def: the sound in coin
the sound in hear

teach.heading: Meet oi
teach.note: Show coin. c-oi-n. oi is usually in the middle of words. Sound buttons: bar under oi.

teach.heading: Meet ear
teach.note: ear is a trigraph. Show hear: h-ear. Ask: ‘What do we hear with?’ Children touch their ears. Mention that ear can also be in ‘bear’ with a different sound; for now teach hear, near.

teach.heading: Read oi and ear words
teach.note: Sound-talk and blend each word. Include meaning questions: ‘What do you spend?’ (coin).

teach.heading: Write oi and ear words
teach.note: Model hear and coin. Dictate: boil, near. Children check using sound buttons.

independent: Write sentences: I hear the bell. I have a coin.
Draw a coin and write a caption

lessons.title: A museum label and description of an old toy for our "Our Class" scrapbook
lessons.bigQuestion: How can an object tell us about the past?
objectives: To understand how a label and description tell a reader about an object
successCriteria: All: write a label that names the toy
Most: write two sentences that describe it with adjectives
Some: use a compound word and say what the toy was used for
lessons.crossCurricular: History: toys from the past and changes within living memory
lessons.smsc: Social: sharing our family memories respectfully in a class scrapbook

keywords.def: a place where old and special objects are kept for people to see
a short note that names an object
the person who looks after a museum's objects
two words joined to make one: teapot, football

hook.text: Look at an old toy. Who might have played with it? How is it different from toys today?
hook.a: A grandparent; it may be wooden or tin, with no batteries or screen.

resources: Tarbiyyah Primary English scheme of work, Memory Box: Express (create a scrapbook called Our Class; each pupil adds a page)
An old toy from home (borrowed from a grandparent or parent, with permission), or a photograph of one from a museum website
Museum label frame: Name, Made of, Used for, How old
Display: compound words
Exercise book

teach.heading: What is a museum label?
teach.note: Show a photograph of a museum label next to an old wooden toy. Read it together.

teach.heading: Compound words
teach.note: Two small words make one big word.

teach.heading: Model: my label
teach.note: Write live as the curator. Say each sentence first.

steps: Made of: It is made of wood and painted red.
Used for: Children spun it on the floor.
How old: It is older than my grandad.

teach.heading: Hinge: label or story?
teach.note: Teams poll.

check.q: Which sentence belongs on a museum label?
options: Once upon a time a top could talk.
This toy is made of wood.
check.why: A label gives facts about the object. A is a story; C is not about the toy.

practice.model: I do: two small words, rain and coat, join to make one word: raincoat.

practice.q: Write an adjective for an old wooden toy

practice.a: For example: It is made of tin.

independent.q: Core: write a museum label for your old toy: its name, what it is made of and what it was used for
independent.a: For example: A tin car. It is made of metal. Children pushed it along the floor.
independent.model: Labelled model: Name: A rocking horse | Made of: It is made of wood. | Describe (adjectives): It has a soft, long tail. | Used for: Children rocked on it.

independent.q: Extend: add a sentence with a compound word
independent.a: For example: It was kept in the cupboard.

independent.q: Stretch: write how it is different from a toy today
independent.a: For example: It has no batteries.

exit.q: What does a museum label tell you?
exit.a: What the object is and facts about it

lessons.homework: Ask a grown-up about a toy they played with when they were young. Tell the class about it next lesson.
lessons.send: SEND: label frame with word bank (wood, metal, plastic; spin, push, roll). EAL: name the object and its material aloud before writing. Stretch: write a question someone at the museum might ask about the toy and answer it.
